analyst_view.overall: Nottingham Forest (17th, 9 pts, two wins in 11, last game a 2-0 defeat at Bournemouth) host Chelsea (8th, 16 pts, four defeats in five including 4-1 at home to Leeds) on Friday night, with both Oliver Glasner and Xabi Alonso under pressure. Forest are without Nicolò Savona and Nicolás Domínguez, as the numbers assume, while Callum Hudson-Odoi is back in training and may make the bench and Xaver Schlager is in contention; previews no longer list Igor Jesus as out, though nobody confirms his fitness. Chelsea are still without Joao Pedro, Reece James, Maxence Lacroix and Jorrel Hato (the numbers already take Joao Pedro's goals off, -18.4%), Jamie Gittens is not match-fit, and the newest news is that Moisés Caicedo and Wesley Fofana are available after Alonso's Thursday update (one report, Yahoo Sports, 26 Nov; earlier previews had Caicedo as a doubt). Andy Madley referees (3.7 cards a game, already counted) and neither side played midweek, so the only change from yesterday is a small one: Caicedo's return.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, 1.5 for Forest and 1.1 for Chelsea, and already take Joao Pedro's share off Chelsea (-18.4%), with Emegha expected to lead the line again after scoring against Leeds. Forest have only nine league goals and three in five home games, but Chelsea's patched-up back line (Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill, Chavarria) has just let in four, so the two weaknesses pull against each other. Caicedo's return helps Chelsea protect that back line a little, but not enough to move the total, so I stay at 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 4.9 each, already adding a little for Forest's recent corner count and taking 5% off Chelsea's quieter run. Without Reece James and with Gittens still short of fitness, Chelsea have less width, but both have been out for weeks, so that is in their recent figures already; Forest still have no set-piece goal this season, which does not change how many corners they win. Nothing new moves corners, so I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards and already take 7.7% off for Andy Madley (3.7 a game) and allow for Chelsea's quieter recent run. Yesterday I set Caicedo's likely absence against the tension of two managers under pressure in a game Forest need for their relegation fight; one report (Yahoo Sports, 26 Nov) now says Caicedo is available, and the numbers made no card adjustment for him being out, so his usual fouling in midfield comes back on top of that tension. A mild lean up of 4%, to about 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots, 14.7 for Forest, and already add 13% after Forest's 99 shots in their last six. With Caicedo reported fit to start beside Lavia, Chelsea's midfield is stronger than the Henderson-Lavia pair previews expected, so Gibbs-White and Ndoye should find a little less room, and Forest's recent shot spree (one on target from 17 at Bournemouth) included plenty of low-value efforts. A small trim of 3%, to about 25.3, since the Caicedo news rests on one report.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. Forest shoot often but land few and lean on Liam Delap up front, while Chelsea hit the target fairly often even without Joao Pedro, whose absence is already in their figures. Caicedo's return trims Forest's shots slightly but hardly changes how many reach the goalkeeper, so I stay at 8.6.
